packet.headline_seed: Chamath Palihapitiya raises $135M Series A for his AI coding startup, takes CEO role
packet.description_seed: VCs remain thirsty to fund AI coding startups. This one, founded by investor Chamath Palihapitiya, is no exception.

what: Chamath Palihapitiya raises $135M Series A for his AI coding startup, takes CEO role

clean_source_blocks.text: VCs remain thirsty to fund AI coding startups. This one, founded by investor Chamath Palihapitiya, is no exception.

Chamath Palihapitiya, best known for his venture capital firm Social Capital and the All-In podcast, announced Monday that the AI coding startup he founded raised a sizable Series A. The company, 8090 Labs, closed a $135 million round led by Salesforce Ventures with participation from Jeffrey Katzenberg’s WndrCo; David Sacks’ Craft Ventures; fellow All-In hosts and “besties” David Friedberg (The Production Board) and Jason Calacanis (Launch); and angel investors like Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora and Quora CEO Adam D’Angelo. ---

On The Axios Show, Chamath Palihapitiya said Meta “fumbled” its lead in AI, dismissed the jobs apocalypse, and finally called his SPAC incentives “grossly misaligned.” Here is what the investor told Axios. Chamath Palihapitiya does not do quiet interviews. On The Axios Show, the investor and All-In podcast co-host ranged across Meta’s AI stumble, the future of work, his own SPAC regrets and the limits of online privacy. His views matter. They carry weight in the White House and with hundreds of thousands of podcast listeners. Few investors swing as freely between tech, markets and politics. Palihapitiya is an unusual messenger. He is an immigrant, a Trump supporter and a former Facebook executive who helped build the company. That mix gave the conversation an edge. He did not spare his old employer.

He framed the AI market as three pillars. One pillar covers the closed American labs, OpenAI and Anthropic. Another holds China’s cheaper open-weight challengers, led by DeepSeek. The third stood there for Meta to take: the open-source, open-weight American lab. Meta’s Llama models count as open weight, not fully open source. He believes the company failed to own that lane, and it now leans toward proprietary models instead. He declined to guess why. Palihapitiya said he does not know enough about Meta’s internal decisions to explain the stumble. He just sees the result. The stakes are large. Meta has poured billions into AI research and talent. Yet his point is about position, not spend. The company that mastered social distribution, he argued, failed to turn that edge into AI leadership.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: TechCrunch]
Chamath Palihapitiya, best known for his venture capital firm Social Capital and the All-In podcast, announced Monday that the AI coding startup he founded raised a sizable Series A.

The company, 8090 Labs, closed a $135 million round led by Salesforce Ventures with participation from Jeffrey Katzenberg’s WndrCo; David Sacks’ Craft Ventures; fellow All-In hosts and “besties” David Friedberg (The Production Board) and Jason Calacanis (Launch); and angel investors like Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora and Quora CEO Adam D’Angelo.

---

[Lähde: The Next Web]
On The Axios Show, Chamath Palihapitiya said Meta “fumbled” its lead in AI, dismissed the jobs apocalypse, and finally called his SPAC incentives “grossly misaligned.” Here is what the investor told Axios.

Chamath Palihapitiya does not do quiet interviews. On The Axios Show, the investor and All-In podcast co-host ranged across Meta’s AI stumble, the future of work, his own SPAC regrets and the limits of online privacy. His views matter. They carry weight in the White House and with hundreds of thousands of podcast listeners. Few investors swing as freely between tech, markets and politics.

Palihapitiya is an unusual messenger. He is an immigrant, a Trump supporter and a former Facebook executive who helped build the company. That mix gave the conversation an edge. He did not spare his old employer.

He saved his sharpest words for Facebook. The company “completely fumbled” a huge chance to lead in AI, he told Axios’ Dan Primack. He even said it had “profoundly failed.”

The critique stings because of his history. Back in 2022, before ChatGPT launched, Palihapitiya argued Meta held a strong position in AI. The company knew so much about its users. It had the data and the reach to match.

Then the moment arrived, and Meta missed it. When chatbot mania hit, Facebook had the distribution to push AI products to billions of people at once. It could have become the champion of open-weight AI. Instead, he argued, Nvidia and Jensen Huang read the moment better and built the ecosystem around open models.

He framed the AI market as three pillars. One pillar covers the closed American labs, OpenAI and Anthropic. Another holds China’s cheaper open-weight challengers, led by DeepSeek. The third stood there for Meta to take: the open-source, open-weight American lab. Meta’s Llama models count as open weight, not fully open source. He believes the company failed to own that lane, and it now leans toward proprietary models instead.

He declined to guess why. Palihapitiya said he does not know enough about Meta’s internal decisions to explain the stumble. He just sees the result.

The stakes are large. Meta has poured billions into AI research and talent. Yet his point is about position, not spend. The company that mastered social distribution, he argued, failed to turn that edge into AI leadership.

On work, he pushed back hard against the doom. The idea that AI will erase jobs makes an “incredible headline,” he said. But he thinks it ignores history.

Primack floated

payload.title: Chamath Palihapitiyan 8090 Labs keräsi 135 miljoonan dollarin rahoituksen
payload.summary: Sijoittaja Chamath Palihapitiyan perustama 8090 Labs on kerännyt 135 miljoonan dollarin A-sarjan rahoituksen. Kierrosta johti Salesforce Ventures, ja mukana oli useita tunnettuja teknologia- ja pääomasijoittajia.
payload.content:
Chamath Palihapitiyan perustama tekoälykoodaukseen keskittyvä startup 8090 Labs on kerännyt 135 miljoonan dollarin A-sarjan rahoituksen. Social Capital -sijoitusyhtiöstä ja All-In-podcastista tunnettu Palihapitiya ilmoitti rahoituksesta maanantaina ja on ottanut yhtiössä toimitusjohtajan roolin.

## Rahoituskierros kokosi tunnettuja sijoittajia

8090 Labsin A-sarjan rahoituskierrosta johti Salesforce Ventures. Mukana olivat myös Jeffrey Katzenbergin WndrCo, David Sacksin Craft Ventures sekä Palihapitiyan All-In-podcastista tutut David Friedbergin The Production Board ja Jason Calacanisin Launch.

Rahoittajajoukkoon kuului lisäksi enkelisijoittajia, kuten Palo Alto Networksin toimitusjohtaja Nikesh Arora ja Quoran toimitusjohtaja Adam D’Angelo. Lähdeaineiston mukaan pääomasijoittajien kiinnostus tekoälykoodauksen startup-yhtiöihin on yhä vahvaa, ja 8090 Labsin kierros kuvataan tästä yhtenä esimerkkinä.

Yhtiöstä kerrotut tiedot jäävät rajallisiksi: paketissa vahvistetaan perustaja, rahoituksen koko, kierroksen johtaja, osallistuneet sijoittajat ja Palihapitiyan toimitusjohtajarooli. Sen sijaan 8090 Labsin tuotteesta, asiakkaista tai tarkemmasta strategiasta ei anneta yksityiskohtia.

## Palihapitiyan tausta tuo yhtiölle näkyvyyttä

Palihapitiya on näkyvä hahmo teknologian, pääomasijoittamisen ja politiikkaa sivuavan markkinakeskustelun rajapinnassa. Hänet tunnetaan myös entisenä Facebook-johtajana, ja Axiosin haastattelussa hän arvioi laajasti tekoälymarkkinan rakennetta, työn tulevaisuutta, SPAC-kannustimia ja verkkoyksityisyyden rajoja.

Samassa haastattelussa Palihapitiya sanoi Metan epäonnistuneen tekoälyetumatkansa hyödyntämisessä. Hänen mukaansa tekoälymarkkina rakentuu kolmen pilarin varaan: suljettuihin yhdysvaltalaisiin laboratorioihin, kuten OpenAIhin ja Anthropiciin, Kiinan edullisempiin avoimen painotuksen haastajiin, kuten DeepSeekiin, sekä yhdysvaltalaiseen avoimen lähdekoodin tai avoimen painotuksen vaihtoehtoon.

Palihapitiyan mukaan Meta olisi voinut omia tämän kolmannen aseman, vaikka sen Llama-mallit ovat hänen kuvauksessaan avoimen painotuksen eivätkä täysin avoimen lähdekoodin malleja. Hän ei väittänyt tietävänsä Metan sisäisiä päätöksiä, vaan sanoi näkevänsä lopputuloksen: hänen arvionsa mukaan kyse on enemmän asemoinnista kuin pelkästä rahankäytöstä.
